about: Research prose behind each built-in device model's animation figures: what the API does, its risks, and the sources. scripts/ci/led-fixtures.mjs merges these into scripts/ci/tests/fixtures/device-models.json as `animation.notes` / `animation.sources`; the runtime built-ins in src/lib/devices.ts deliberately carry neither, so the bundle holds only what rendering needs. `unverified` in a note marks a memory.

vestaboard_flagship.notes: The hardware cascades by itself (~16 ms per flap at 60 RPM); a client sends one message, never frames.

vestaboard_note.notes: The hardware cascades by itself (~16 ms per flap at 60 RPM); a client sends one message, never frames.

vestaboard_note_array.notes: The hardware cascades by itself (~16 ms per flap at 60 RPM); a client sends one message, never frames.

vestaboard_panel.notes: A virtual board that imitates Note hardware; a client sends one message, never frames.

divoom_pixoo64.notes: Draw/SendHttpGif: one POST per frame (PicNum frames, PicOffset index, PicSpeed ms, PicData base64 RGB888, PicWidth must be 64), played locally. HARDWARE TEST on a Pixoo 64 (FiestaBoard program, 2026-10-04): an uploaded animation LOOPS forever (there is no play-once); more than ~3 uploaded frames first show a ~6 s 'LOADING…' overlay; landing on a still after an animation glitches for ~5 s; a single-frame push is clean in ~0.5 s; 40 frames play and ~55 is the most it takes. So the Pixoo SNAPS: one frame per change, modelled as stream at a nominal 2 fps (below every animated entry's minimum, so the default transition is none), and an adapter never uploads a sequence. This measurement supersedes the earlier community figures (a 32-frame cap, a ~300-push freeze, a ~5 s overlay) kept in the sources for reference.
sources: hardware test on a Pixoo 64, FiestaBoard program, 2026-10-04

ulanzi_tc001_awtrix.notes: Custom apps take `draw` ops (dp/dl/dr/df/dc/dfc/dt/db) over HTTP or MQTT; `db` with a full 8×32 bitmap returned ErrorParsingJson (#214). TSPEED (app transition) defaults to 500 ms, ATIME 7 s. No stated rate limit; the push rate is UNMEASURED (no test device), so the model is held at a nominal 2 fps — below every animated entry's minimum — and stays on snap, letting the firmware's own Slide transition carry the change.

wled_32x32.notes: DDP on UDP 4048 (480 RGB pixels per 1440-byte datagram; 1024 LEDs = 3 datagrams a frame) holds 25–40 fps on an ESP32; E1.31 is documented at '25 ms (40 fps)' for ≤ 510 LEDs; WLED_FPS default 42. The JSON `seg.i` route is HTTP + parse per call and not for this.

hub75_64x32.notes: rpi-rgb-led-matrix refreshes 'typically in the hundreds of Hertz' (three 128×64 panels: 410 Hz); a Pi daemon fed over the network (flaschen-taschen style) holds 30–60 fps.

hub75_128x64.notes: As hub75_64x32; a 128×64 chain still refreshes above 100 Hz on a Pi 4.

max7219_4in1.notes: A 32×8 frame is 32 bytes over SPI; MD_Parola's setSpeed() runs animations at any ms interval ('zero to run as fast as possible'). Hundreds of fps locally (unverified figure); the bridge from a host to the module is custom, so the figure assumes you own it.

p10_hub12_32x16.notes: HUB12 modules are scanned by the host microcontroller (DMD32 / DMD_STM32, 30–70 µs row on-time); a frame over serial is 64 bytes. No standard host protocol, so the figure assumes you own the bridge.

tidbyt_tronbyt.notes: Tronbyt server: POST /v0/devices/{id}/push with a base64 WebP, displayTimeSec default 30; devices poll /next and loop the animation. Pixlet render.Root(delay=ms) sets the frame time (50 ms default — unverified). Tidbyt's cloud is rate-limited with no published number. One WebP per message change, so a flip is a sequence at 80 ms per step with no half-flaps.
